metadata.title: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP07 Feature Search
metadata.description: Pattern Recognition, Feature Selection unit, KP07 feature search; guided v1; English self-study; answer first then feedback

scene-root.name: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP07 Feature Search

scene-u01.name: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP07 Feature Search

p01-cost-title.name: p01-cost-title
p01-cost-title.text: No enumeration: how many sets do the three methods evaluate?

p01-cost-ctx.name: p01-cost-ctx
p01-cost-ctx.text: Choose $l$ from $m$ features. Bar length = $\log_{10}$ of the number of evaluations (log axis): exhaustive is $\binom{m}{l}$; forward and backward (SFS, SBS) use the textbook formulas.

p01-cost-xc.name: p01-cost-xc
p01-cost-xc.text: Log axis: each big tick to the right multiplies the count by 100; the bar length is the number of digits, not the count itself

p01-cost-cm.name: p01-cost-cm
p01-cost-cm.text: Exhaustive is 1.8×10¹⁰ times forward, yet on the chart they differ by only about 10 ticks (log axis); at $m=5$ greedy search saves nothing over exhaustive (12 vs 10)

p02-board-title.name: p02-board-title
p02-board-title.text: The shared toy problem: choose 3 of 5 features; every subset has a score $J$

p02-board-ctx.name: p02-board-ctx
p02-board-ctx.text: Each circle shows a subset and its score $J$ (the larger the better). The next three pages all walk on this board. Adding a feature never lowers the score (monotone).

p02-board-bt.name: p02-board-bt
p02-board-bt.text: The globally best three features are $\{B,D,E\}$: $J=95$

p03-sfs-title.name: p03-sfs-title
p03-sfs-title.text: Forward selection (SFS): add the best one each time; a choice cannot be taken back

p03-sfs-ctx.name: p03-sfs-ctx
p03-sfs-ctx.text: At each step choose the highest score among "the chosen ones plus one"; red is the path it walked.

p03-sfs-t1.name: p03-sfs-t1
p03-sfs-t1.text: Step 1: among single features $A=40$ is highest, choose $A$

p03-sfs-res.name: p03-sfs-res
p03-sfs-res.text: SFS stops at $ABD$ ($J=88$) with 12 evaluations; it misses the globally best $BDE$ ($95$) circled in green

p04-sbs-title.name: p04-sbs-title
p04-sbs-title.text: Backward selection (SBS): start from all, drop the most useless one each time

p04-sbs-ctx.name: p04-sbs-ctx
p04-sbs-ctx.text: Arrow = drop one feature; at each step compare the score left after dropping each one (the thick green arrow and green pill are the chosen, the grey dashed ones are eliminated).

p04-sbs-res.name: p04-sbs-res
p04-sbs-res.text: SBS finds $BDE$ ($J=95$) with 10 evaluations ($=1+5+4$), the same as the global best

p04-sbs-cv.name: p04-sbs-cv
p04-sbs-cv.text: This time backward succeeds and forward fails, which is the result of this set of numbers, not a rule; backward also cannot take decisions back (dropped ones never return)

p05-sffs-title.name: p05-sffs-title
p05-sffs-title.text: Floating search (SFFS): after adding, look back and swap out old ones

p05-sffs-ctx.name: p05-sffs-ctx
p05-sffs-ctx.text: The first three steps are the same as SFS (red); after $ABD$ there is an extra "look-back check".

p05-sffs-t2.name: p05-sffs-t2
p05-sffs-t2.text: Look-back check: remove $A$, $BD=75$ exceeds the historical best two-feature set $AD=65$, so $A$ is removed

p05-sffs-t3.name: p05-sffs-t3
p05-sffs-t3.text: Then add forward: add the best $E$ to $BD$ ⇒ $BDE=95$

p05-sffs-res.name: p05-sffs-res
p05-sffs-res.text: SFFS finds $BDE$ ($J=95$) with 21 evaluations (more than the 12 of SFS)

p05-sffs-cv.name: p05-sffs-cv
p05-sffs-cv.text: This example is deliberately designed: the textbook says clearly that floating search "does not guarantee finding all the best subsets"

p06-mono-title.name: p06-mono-title
p06-mono-title.text: To guarantee the optimum: scores must not fall when features are added, so we can prune

p06-mono-ctx.name: p06-mono-ctx
p06-mono-ctx.text: Monotonicity: $J(x_1,\dots,x_i)\le J(x_1,\dots,x_i,x_{i+1})$. The scores on the board satisfy it.

p06-mono-bt.name: p06-mono-bt
p06-mono-bt.text: Adding one more feature each time to the right: the score only rises, never falls (monotone)

p06-mono-cg2.name: p06-mono-cg2
p06-mono-cg2.text:
One branch: even adding
all the rest reaches only here

p06-mono-g3.name: p06-mono-g3
p06-mono-g3.text: $70<85$ ⇒ this whole branch can be pruned without trying its members

p06-mono-wr.name: p06-mono-wr
p06-mono-wr.text: The validation accuracy of a wrapper is usually not monotone (KP06: beyond a certain number of features the validation error rises), so branch and bound is mostly used with the separability criteria of a filter; with many features it is still too slow

p07-compare-title.name: p07-compare-title
p07-compare-title.text: Results of the four methods on the same problem

p07-compare-ctx.name: p07-compare-ctx
p07-compare-ctx.text: Left: score $J$ of the 3 chosen features; right: evaluations. Bars start at 0, proportional to values; green dashed line = global best 95.

p07-compare-hj.name: p07-compare-hj
p07-compare-hj.text: Left: score J of the chosen features (bar length = J)

p07-compare-he.name: p07-compare-he
p07-compare-he.text: Right: number of evaluations (bar length = count)

p07-compare-ct.name: p07-compare-ct
p07-compare-ct.text: Forward is 7 points short; floating search needs more evaluations (21 vs 12); exhaustive is feasible only with very few features

p08-choose-title.name: p08-choose-title
p08-choose-title.text: How to choose: by number of features, number to keep and scoring cost

p08-choose-ctx.name: p08-choose-ctx
p08-choose-ctx.text: Rule-of-thumb map: top to bottom = total features $m$; left to right in the middle row = fraction kept $l$; borders are illustrative, no method is always best.

p08-choose-xc.name: p08-choose-xc
p08-choose-xc.text: Middle row: left = keep very few ($l$ far below $m$), middle = about half, right = nearly all ($l$ close to $m$)

p08-choose-lA.name: p08-choose-lA
p08-choose-lA.text:
Thousands of features: first cut to a few dozen with a filter or forward selection
then refine with the methods below

p08-choose-lBf.name: p08-choose-lBf
p08-choose-lBf.text:
Few to keep
($l$ far below $m$) ⇒ use forward
fewer evaluations

p08-choose-lBm.name: p08-choose-lBm
p08-choose-lBm.text:
About half to keep
⇒ forward or backward both fine
similar counts

p08-choose-lBb.name: p08-choose-lBb
p08-choose-lBb.text:
Nearly all to keep
($l$ close to $m$) ⇒ use backward
fewer evaluations

p08-choose-lF.name: p08-choose-lF
p08-choose-lF.text: Cheap scoring and you want better: any of the above can switch to floating search (can go back)

p08-choose-lC.name: p08-choose-lC
p08-choose-lC.text: Few features and a monotone criterion: only then consider branch and bound, which guarantees the optimum

p08-choose-nt.name: p08-choose-nt
p08-choose-nt.text: The search method and the scoring method are both needed: if the scoring criterion is wrong, however good the search, it only finds the wrong answer more efficiently; the selection itself must also be put inside validation (KP06)

p09-sk-ctx.name: p09-sk-ctx
p09-sk-ctx.text: The simulated data of KP06 (5 features, choose 3, linear discriminant classifier, 5 folds). The bars on the right start at 0 and are proportional to accuracy.

p09-sk-code.name: p09-sk-code
p09-sk-code.text:
```
from sklearn.feature_selection import SequentialFeatureSelector
from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis

sfs = SequentialFeatureSelector(LinearDiscriminantAnalysis(),
          n_features_to_select=3, direction='forward', cv=5)
sfs.fit(X, y)
sfs.get_support()      # the selected features
```

p09-sk-ah.name: p09-sk-ah
p09-sk-ah.text: Accuracy on new data (bars start at 0)

p09-sk-nt.name: p09-sk-nt
p09-sk-nt.text: Both forward and backward choose $\{x_2,x_4,x_5\}$; $x_1$ and $x_2$ are almost duplicates, so swapping them does not matter. The wrapper finds $x_5$, which is useless alone

p10-practice1-title.name: p10-practice1-title
p10-practice1-title.text: Exercise 1: choose 3 of 50 features; how many evaluations does each of the three methods need?

p10-practice1-ctx.name: p10-practice1-ctx
p10-practice1-ctx.text: Work it out yourself first and guess on the log axis where the three bars will stop; then press Next for feedback.

p10-practice1-q1.name: p10-practice1-q1
p10-practice1-q1.text: Exercise 1: $m=50$ features, choose $l=3$. How many evaluations do exhaustive, SFS and SBS need?

p10-practice1-xc.name: p10-practice1-xc
p10-practice1-xc.text: Log axis: each tick to the right multiplies the count by 10

p10-practice1-cm.name: p10-practice1-cm
p10-practice1-cm.text: With $l$ very small, forward is cheapest (147); backward must first evaluate large subsets and is much more costly (1,270)

p11-practice2-title.name: p11-practice2-title
p11-practice2-title.text: Exercise 2: three features, choose two; does SFS choose correctly?

p11-practice2-ctx.name: p11-practice2-ctx
p11-practice2-ctx.text: Work it out yourself first, then press Next for feedback.

p11-practice2-q2.name: p11-practice2-q2
p11-practice2-q2.text: Exercise 2: three features $A,B,C$, choose 2. Single features: $A{:}30,\ B{:}25,\ C{:}20$; pairs: $AB{:}40,\ AC{:}38,\ BC{:}55$. What does SFS choose? What is the optimum?

p11-practice2-a1.name: p11-practice2-a1
p11-practice2-a1.text:
SFS: the first step chooses $A$ (30, highest)
The second step chooses $AB$ among $AB{:}40$ and $AC{:}38$

p11-practice2-a2.name: p11-practice2-a2
p11-practice2-a2.text:
Exhaustive: the optimum is $BC$ ($J=55$)
$SFS$ missed it

p11-practice2-cm.name: p11-practice2-cm
p11-practice2-cm.text: This is the nesting effect: $A$ is strongest alone, yet misses the combination of $B$ and $C$

p12-summary-title.name: p12-summary-title
p12-summary-title.text: The whole KP07: when we cannot enumerate, walk greedily; floating can go back, the optimum needs monotonicity

p12-summary-ctx.name: p12-summary-ctx
p12-summary-ctx.text: One chart holds the whole unit: upper left is why greedy, on the right the results of three methods (bar length = J, proportional to the value), below is how to guarantee the optimum and how to choose.

p12-summary-mf.name: p12-summary-mf
p12-summary-mf.text:
Forward SFS · 12 evals
nesting effect, misses 95

p12-summary-mb.name: p12-summary-mb
p12-summary-mb.text:
Backward SBS · 10 evals
dropped ones never return

p12-summary-mw.name: p12-summary-mw
p12-summary-mw.text:
Floating SFFS · 21 evals
can go back, no guarantee of optimum

p12-summary-o0.name: p12-summary-o0
p12-summary-o0.text: To guarantee the optimum: branch and bound needs "adding a feature never lowers the score" (monotone): upper bound 70 < best so far 85 ⇒ prune the branch; a wrapper is usually not monotone

p12-summary-pk.name: p12-summary-pk
p12-summary-pk.text: How to choose: cut first when $m$ is in the thousands; use forward for small $l$; backward for $l$ near $m$; add floating when scoring is cheap

p12-summary-nx.name: p12-summary-nx
p12-summary-nx.text:
The feature selection unit ends here:
we only select existing features
Next unit: can we combine and
transform them into better new features? ⇒ Feature generation
